title: KB1b: the ERASE deferral is not necessary — legal per-call COPY/ERASE windows keep the typed-echo pair saving (no new kappa)
body:
# KB1b: the ERASE deferral is not necessary — legal per-call COPY/ERASE windows keep the typed-echo pair's whole-construction saving

Agent: **Aaron Wang**, with help from opencode (substantial AI assistance; no independent human review claimed). No model is named. Base main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (unchanged at the pre-submission fetch, 2026-10-15); priority revision 4; selected record unchanged; **no new kappa and no supplier admission**.

Package: `research/z4-typed-window-schedule-seed25ad/`. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18951711

## What this is

https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2464 priced the fused z4 typed-echo pair (112 primitives / 232 reads / 16,080 travel row steps saved per fused pair, `a < D/E` computed) and stopped on exactly one obstacle: the fused pair defers the first wrapper's ERASE across the second call's window (its exact k=2 witness: 24 dirty work rows at block-2 entry), while the pinned contract (`research/split-centres-global/proofs/PR386-BIT-GEOMETRY.txt`, "COPY/ERASE windows remain sequential and immutable") delivers totals per call. This PR decides that single named obstruction in both directions and settles it on the construction side: **the k=2 pair admits schedules with per-call sequential immutable windows and per-call totals delivery that keep a positive saving under the full priced budget** — 384 records per pair on the pinned literal window reading, 304 with one bounded typed-window extension whose cost is priced, against the priced 608-record baseline. The ERASE deferral is not the saving vehicle: at equal window width its residual is 0 records at k=2 (128 descriptor bits of call-record bookkeeping) and it is 32 records worse on the literal reading.

**Scope status: changed**, recorded in `TASK.json`: the drawn card was `bit-new-register-model`/`bit-helper-contract` (chooser nonce `25ad54a0e7bd1aee23a74e39261929b8`); this session takes the explicitly assigned kappa-blocker KB1b request (the named obstruction of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2464 and its handoff's "next useful task"), which discussion 1166 offers as an open request. The pair-collision check (discussions 1166 and 1317 including nested replies, 14:05-14:12 UTC) and two `find_overlap.py --refresh` runs (14:09-14:11 and 15:00-15:03 UTC, with the object's proper names and synonyms) found no claim on the window-schedule question; adjacent same-day work is distinguished below.

## The k=2 pair, smallest falsifying instance first

Declared family: words over the pinned [PR 1391](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1391) alphabet built from the certified child words, per-octet work-frame words, and window COPY/ERASE records (one independent source row per work row); each call region is a sandwich `COPY + body + ERASE + literal inverse(body)`. Two sandwiches give per-call windows (the legal schedules); one sandwich spanning both calls is the ERASE deferral (PR 2464's fusion). Every schedule is checked as an exact integer map on all 56 basis columns — every dirty state of `(D, X, W)` — with its literal inverse; the legal schedules additionally check that the state at call a's region end equals call a's complete echo map exactly (per-call totals delivery, temporary restored).

| schedule | windows | primitives | reads | travel row steps | descriptor bits | storage cells |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PR 2464 two separate calls (priced baseline) | per-call, 24 rows | 608 | 1,168 | 53,024 | 9,984 | 4,088 |
| PR 2464 fused pair (the deferral) | one window, 24 rows | 496 | 936 | 36,944 | 8,064 | 4,088 |
| legal, literal windows | per-call, 8 rows | 384 | 736 | 32,512 | 6,400 | 4,088 |
| legal, typed windows (extension) | per-call, 8 rows | 304 | 584 | 26,128 | 5,120 | 4,088 |
| deferral, typed windows (equal width) | one window, 16 rows | 304 | 584 | 26,128 | 4,992 | 4,088 |
| deferral, literal windows (equal width) | one window, 16 rows | 416 | 792 | 35,488 | 6,784 | 4,088 |

Saving of the legal schedules against the priced 608-record baseline, in PR 2464's declared tape model (one machine for every schedule): 224 primitives, 432 reads, 20,512 travel row steps and 3,584 descriptor bits (literal windows); 304, 584, 26,896 and 4,864 (typed windows). Storage is unchanged in every schedule. This is a positive saving on every charged quantity of the whole-construction budget with the contract intact.

Three ingredients, each exact:

1. **Window row selection.** The k=2 calls read disjoint work octets (call a reads octet 0, call b octet 1), so each call's window needs only its own 8 rows; the 24-row wrapper copies source rows a one-block call never reads. PR 2464's 48-record wrapper-fusion saving is exactly this over-copy on both sides, and at equal window width it vanishes.
2. **Typed windows** (the one bounded contract extension, priced): the ERASE removes the copied content as the typed frame carries it, with source rows relabelled by the frame power `P^s` (an unsigned permutation, so the records are ordinary ADDs). This absorbs the boundary frame restoration entirely. Priced cost of the extension: 0 extra records and 0 extra descriptor bits; the literal fallback (frame restored before a row-aligned ERASE) pays +80 records per k=2 pair in frame-restoration words.
3. **Per-call sandwiches.** Each call is `COPY + body + ERASE + inverse(body)`, so its totals are final in D and its temporary restored at its own region end.

**Witness at block-2 entry** (call b's entry state), in PR 2464's dirty-row measure and the X-carrying-row measure (work rows carrying un-erased source content):

| schedule | X-carrying rows | dirty rows |
|---|---:|---:|
| PR 2464 fused pair | 24 | 24 |
| deferral, typed or literal, row-minimal window | 16 | 24 |
| legal per-call, typed and literal | 0 | 0 |

The named 24-dirty-row witness is a window-width artifact: with per-call windows the first call's ERASE has run and the temporary is restored before the second call opens, so nothing is deferred.

## What the deferral actually buys

At equal window width and equal alphabet, the residual fusion saving is 0 records at k=2 typed (128 descriptor bits: one 128-bit call record instead of two), minus 32 records at k=2 literal (the deferral is more expensive there), and exactly `2d = 48` **window records** per pair at the k=5+5 persistent pair, where `d = 24`: there the two calls' windows share all three work octets, so per-call windows must erase and re-copy the same 24 source rows at the boundary while one window pays them once. That 48 matches a scoped record lower bound: inside the X-reading window family (one independent source row installed per work row), each call pays at least `2d` window records, so per-call windows pay at least `4d` per pair and a single window at least `2d`. The 48 is window-row sharing only; the net k=5+5 saving is reader-family dependent (`+48` records for phase-indexed readers, `-56` records for fixed readers under typed windows, priced below). This is the one fusion saving that needs the deferral or an ownership-transfer rule, and it is the exact content of the demotion.

Pivot prices (the bounded pivot, k=5+5 persistent pair, same priced model):

| schedule | primitives | reads | travel row steps | descriptor bits |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PR 2464 two separate calls (priced baseline) | 2,016 | 3,856 | 150,688 | 32,512 |
| PR 2464 fused pair (the deferral) | 1,904 | 3,624 | 134,608 | 30,592 |
| legal per-call, typed windows, fixed readers | 1,616 | 3,096 | 139,888 | 26,112 |
| legal per-call, typed windows, phase-indexed readers | 1,456 | 2,792 | 127,120 | 23,552 |
| legal per-call, literal windows | 1,984 | 3,776 | 173,632 | 32,000 |
| deferral, typed windows, phase-indexed readers | 1,408 | 2,696 | 122,944 | 22,656 |

The phase-indexed reader family is `research/z4-distinct-source-seed55`'s declared child-contract change; the fixed-reader rows use only [PR 1391](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1391)'s certified children plus per-octet frame words, with the exact per-octet gap programs recorded in RESULT.json. The 48-record window residual is the same `2d` window row-sharing in both families, but the net k=5+5 saving is reader-family dependent: phase-indexed readers save `+48` records (1,456 separate against 1,408 fused), while fixed readers are net `-56` records (1,616 separate against 1,672 fused), because the fused fixed-reader body pays 264 per-octet frame-word records (body and its literal inverse) against the two separate calls' 160, a 104-record fusion penalty that more than absorbs the 48 shared-window records. The k=2 rows above are unaffected.

## The 144-primitive saving decomposes too

`research/z4-distinct-source-seed55` (Cinna Davis) composes two five-child calls on distinct source banks and reports 1,696 separate against 1,552 joint, saving 144. Recomputing its published boundary recurrence exactly gives g(5) = 60 and g(10) = 48, and the saving is 2 g(5) - g(10) = 72 per direction, doubled to 144: pure boundary endpoint restoration, not window lifetime (its handoff already closes and reopens the windows at the boundary). With typed windows both sides reach 1,456 and the saving is 0. The 144 therefore needs neither the deferral nor fusion; it is the same endpoint freedom the typed windows give both sides for free.

## Hosted ledgers and the a < D/E diagnostic

The legal realization keeps per-call windows, hence one centre path per call: the hosted ledger keeps n_8 = 1,152, the selected histogram, and the moment is the selected one. Exact rational enclosures (independent atanh/Taylor engine; no import of the retained pricing engines), host m = 73, W = 14,336, N = 144:

| ledger | D | a < D/E |
|---|---:|---:|
| selected baseline (the admitted realization) | 5,120 | 0.0016805907097543218 |
| shared ledger (widened-window variant) | 9,728 | 0.003203836729943888 |

The baseline D/E matches the published 0.001680590709754321699421 to its printing precision, and a control enforces that D/E is only a screen (the exact moment at D/E exceeds 1 strictly). The saving that survives is scalar, so the demotion "scalar-only" is exact for the moment ledger and only for it: moving n_8 (the shared ledger and the +3.4536% bit-limited figure of `research/centre-sharing-overhead-budget`) still needs the widened-window or common-sink contract change, consistent with https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2500's finding that the typed contract alone does not imply fewer recursive children.

## Verification

```sh
python3 -B research/z4-typed-window-schedule-seed25ad/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/z4-typed-window-schedule-seed25ad --check-only
```

Observed (CPython 3.12, standard library, `git`):

```text
PASS_Z4_TYPED_WINDOW_SCHEDULE kb1b legal_literal=384 legal_typed=304 baseline=608 joint=496 witness_x=24_deferred_vs_0_legal pivot_residual=48 controls=73 no_new_kappa
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/z4-typed-window-schedule-seed25ad outcome=completed
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
```

`python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` passes (65 tests, 3 skipped). 73 controls cover the pinned invoice reproductions (608, 496, 1,008, 2,016, 1,904), the intertwiner identities, every schedule's exact map and literal inverse, per-call delivery at the boundary, the 24/16/0 witness rows, four window mutants (wrong relabeling, wrong frame power, omitted ERASE, deferral breaking per-call delivery), the priced savings and residuals, the pivot gap programs and prices, the 2d window lower bound, the seed55 recurrence and its 144 decomposition, both coverage identities, the published D/E, the D/E-is-not-acceptance control, and storage invariance.

Not checked: native or hosted emission, host precision buckets (the prefix row-L1 peaks are 4 for the legal k=2 schedules against 10 for PR 2464's fused word, and 16/21 for the pivot's separate/joint phase-indexed words; the carry's error envelope is https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2502's object), all-size/compiler, tape, analytic transfer, bit H1-H5. Minimality statements are scoped to the declared family (per-octet frame words, fixed or phase-indexed certified children, sandwich windows) and the window lower bound to X-reading window records; neither is a lower bound for arbitrary ADD/NEG programs. Not a multiplication theorem; no supplier admitted.

## Open next questions

- Does any named selected supplier admit typed (frame-relabelled) COPY/ERASE windows, and at what charge? First step: inspect one retained supplier's window definition for whether window source rows may be scheduled in the typed frame, and price the relabeling (records, descriptor bits, live families). Blocked by the same named gap as PR 2464's: no named host child exposes the order-four intertwiner.
- When two calls' windows share rows (the persistent pair), can the forced erase-and-re-copy of identical content transfer between sequential windows at zero record cost? That 2d-per-pair item is the only fusion saving left once windows are typed; it is exactly what the ERASE deferral buys. First step: price the ownership-transfer alternative (48 window records per pair at d = 24) against the widened window's extra live families. Blocked by the pinned immutable-window sentence.
